papers.title: The Fat-Body Secreted Neuropeptide CCHa2 Signals Insulin-Producing Cells in the Brain to Promote Sleep.
papers.summary: A targeted RNAi screen in Drosophila identified fat-body-enriched, feeding-regulated genes affecting sleep; fat-body CCHa2 knockdown reduced sleep duration and depth, and CCHa2-R knockdown in brain insulin-producing cells recapitulated the sleep-loss phenotype, defining a fat body-IPC axis modulating sleep.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "SleepEEGpy: a Python-based software integration package to organize preprocessing, analysis, and visualization of sleep EEG data" [Comput. Biol. Med. 192, (2025), 110232].
papers.summary: This is a published corrigendum to the SleepEEGpy software paper on a Python-based package for preprocessing, analysis, and visualization of sleep EEG data; the abstract provides no scientific findings.

papers.title: Sleep Renormalizes Negative Emotional Generalization
papers.summary: Using a face-outcome generalization paradigm with immediate and delayed testing after sleep versus wakefulness, plus fMRI and high-density EEG, the study found sleep selectively enhanced positive and reduced negative emotional generalization; amygdala/limbic outcome-processing activity and sleep spindles predicted the sleep-specific shift toward positive generalization.

papers.title: Simvastatin Modulates Astrocyte and Microglial Reactivity and Aggressive Behavior After Chronic Sleep Deprivation in Rats.
authors: José de Anchieta de Castro E Horta-Júnior
papers.summary: In male Wistar rats subjected to 45 days of chronic sleep deprivation via the modified multiple platform method, sleep loss increased aggressive/reactive behavior and astrocytic and microglial reactivity in dorsal hippocampus with shifts toward reactive microglial phenotypes; simvastatin attenuated these glial alterations and modulated selected peripheral cytokines, with limited amygdala effects.

papers.title: Response to "From spectral parameterization to spectral staging in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder".
papers.summary: This is an author response to a commentary on spectral parameterization and spectral staging in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder; the abstract provides no scientific findings.

papers.title: Sleep and Cardiometabolic Disease: A Wearable-Electronic Health Record Study in the US All of Us Research Program.
papers.summary: In a cohort of 10,362 All of Us participants with linked Fitbit and electronic health record data over 180-day baselines, night-to-night variability in sleep duration and timing was associated with increased risk of a CVD composite (HR ~1.20-1.24 per SD), heart failure, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes, whereas mean sleep duration was not associated with the CVD composite; more wearable-estimated sleep cycles were independently associated with lower atrial arrhythmia risk.

papers.title: Novel sleep scoring method for neurodegenerative diseases: feasibility and reliability in advanced Parkinson disease.
papers.summary: Video-polysomnography from 15 Parkinson disease patients and five age-matched controls was scored blind by five raters using a novel methodology incorporating abnormal stages (abnormal Wake, Subwake, Undifferentiated NREM, Poorly Structured N2, abnormal REM); the method showed substantial interrater agreement (kappa = 0.75), comparable to AASM scoring (kappa = 0.73), and abnormal stages occurred mainly in advanced PD with cognitive impairment and motor fluctuations.

papers.title: CircaVal: a gene-centric multi-omics platform for exploring circadian regulatory features.
papers.summary: The authors developed CircaVal, a gene-centric multi-omics platform integrating harmonized public datasets in humans, mice, and baboons to explore circadian regulatory features, introducing an integrated rhythmicity score (IRS) that combines concordance across rhythm-detection methods with cross-dataset reproducibility.

papers.title: A multimodal dataset of EEG, eye-tracking, and physiological signals during naturalistic smartphone interactions
papers.summary: This resource presents a publicly available multimodal dataset (OpenNeuro ds007537, BIDS-formatted) of synchronized 64-channel EEG, eye-tracking, PPG, and galvanic skin response recordings from 23 participants during 10 minutes of naturalistic smartphone use and a subsequent 5-minute nature-video relaxation condition, with smartphone addiction and problematic-use questionnaires.

papers.title: Respiratory self-similarity is a sleep apnea endotype that predicts cardiovascular disease related mortality.
papers.summary: In secondary analyses of the Sleep Heart Health Study and Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, high respiratory self-similarity (a marker of high loop gain) was associated with incident CVD (HR 1.693 in MESA; HR 1.240 in SHHS) and CVD mortality (HR 1.429 and 1.176), associations that were more apparent in men and attenuated with continuous age adjustment.

papers.title: High-frequency EEG activity moderates the association between amyloid burden and tau in cognitively normal adults
papers.summary: In a pilot study of cognitively normal older adults with amyloid PET (20 also with tau PET), higher amyloid burden was associated with higher parietal periodic gamma power, and periodic gamma moderated the amyloid–tau association (p=0.012), with gamma related to entorhinal tau only in amyloid-positive adults. Periodic gamma is proposed as a candidate EEG marker of amyloid-related excitatory-inhibitory imbalance.

papers.title: Sleep architecture disruption and coordinated patterns of inflammatory and extracellular matrix biomarkers in obstructive sleep apnea: a cross-sectional study.
papers.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: In 70 adults with OSA, severe disease was associated with higher TNF-α, IL-6, MMP-2, MMP-9, desmosine, and cellular fibronectin, and these biomarkers correlated with AHI, oxygen desaturation burden, and shorter N3 sleep, forming a densely connected BMI-adjusted inflammatory-ECM cluster. Oxidative stress markers (GSH, MDA) showed weaker, more isolated associations.

papers.title: Diagnostic value of extending outpatient EEG to record sleep - A retrospective study.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: In a retrospective analysis of 1762 extended (~40–50 min) outpatient EEGs without sleep deprivation, N2 sleep was achieved in 70.5% of patients, rising with recording duration, and sleep added unique interictal epileptiform discharges beyond wakefulness (29% vs. an additional 12%), with higher yield particularly in idiopathic generalized epilepsy and self-limited epilepsies.

papers.title: Exercise and physiological monitoring in isolated, confined and extreme environments and space analogues: A scoping review.
papers.summary: This scoping review (17 studies, 2003–2025) mapped exercise and physiological monitoring in isolated, confined and extreme environments and space analogues, finding exercise a pragmatic but domain-specific countermeasure against deconditioning with heterogeneity in exposure, dose, and monitoring limiting comparability.

papers.title: The relevance of sleep and chronopsychology in understanding maladaptive behaviors in eating disorders: A narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that delayed sleep timing, eveningness, insomnia, and circadian misalignment co-occur with disordered eating across anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, orthorexia, and night eating syndrome, with overlapping reward-driven and neuroendocrine mechanisms; preliminary chronotherapeutic interventions (light exposure, sleep phase modification) remain insufficiently tested.

papers.title: Adjunctive perampanel in children with focal-onset seizures and developmental delay or intellectual disability: efficacy, tolerability, and sleep benefits.
papers.summary: In a retrospective single-cohort study of 57 children with focal-onset seizures and developmental delay/intellectual disability (91.2% drug-resistant), adjunctive perampanel achieved responder rates (≥50% seizure reduction) of 89.5%, 81.1%, and 74.5% at 3, 6, and 12 months, with seizure-free rates of 45.6%, 49.1%, and 43.1%; among 29 patients with preexisting sleep disturbance, 93.1% improved.

papers.title: Diaphragm Weakness and Sleep-Related Breathing Disorders in Patients with Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy.
papers.summary: In a prospective study of 16 patients with biopsy-confirmed idiopathic inflammatory myopathies, 25% showed findings suggestive of diaphragm weakness (all with dermatomyositis), and all 11 patients who underwent polysomnography had obstructive sleep apnea (2 severe, 4 moderate, 5 mild).

papers.title: Autonomic Reactivity and EEG-defined Clusters Reveal Distinct Chronic Pain Profiles.
papers.summary: In 177 patients with chronic pain after spine surgery, integrating stress-related heart rate variability (HRV) with resting-state EEG features revealed two EEG clusters and a nominally significant HRV-by-EEG interaction (p=0.030) on pain scores, with higher pain in the LF/HF-decrease group within one EEG cluster; findings were exploratory and require validation.

papers.title: DECAPPING PROTEIN 5 regulates the circadian clock in Arabidopsis
papers.summary: In Arabidopsis, a meta-analysis of mRNA decay datasets showed that high-amplitude clock-controlled genes have shorter half-lives, and iCLIP revealed that DECAPPING PROTEIN 5 (DCP5) binds AU-rich motifs in their 3' UTRs to modulate stability; the dcp5 mutant exhibits an extended circadian period.

papers.title: Wearable Evidence Linking Dyskinesia Burden to Sleep Quality in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.summary: In 47 people with Parkinson's disease, wearable-derived dyskinesia (median DKS) independently predicted poorer sleep quality after adjusting for levodopa dose (B=0.18, p=0.047), whereas clinician-rated dyskinesia did not, supporting wearable monitoring.

papers.title: Probable Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder Associated With Escitalopram in a Patient With Schizoaffective Disorder: A Case Report.
papers.summary: Reports a 46-year-old man with schizoaffective disorder who developed probable REM sleep behavior disorder (dream enactment, sleep paralysis, daytime sleepiness) about 14 months after starting escitalopram 5 mg, with episodes resolving after escitalopram withdrawal and clonazepam initiation and no recurrence at later follow-up.

papers.title: Eyes-open resting-state EEG microstate analysis using ratio-normalized parameters across four- and seven-class solutions in healthy controls, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: Compared ratio-normalized eyes-open resting-state EEG microstate parameters across four- and seven-class solutions in 180 participants (healthy controls, MCI, AD), finding that in the four-class solution MCI showed higher visual-network and lower executive-network microstate engagement than AD, though no effects survived FDR correction.

papers.title: Ultrasonographic assessment of diaphragmatic functions in relation to obstructive sleep apnea severity.
papers.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
papers.summary: In a prospective cross-sectional study of 62 patients with suspected obstructive sleep apnea, ultrasonographic diaphragmatic assessment showed largely preserved function, with left diaphragmatic excursion weakly correlated with AHI and independently associated with OSA severity (AUC 0.72 for moderate-to-severe OSA).

papers.title: Neurodevelopmental outcomes of infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia: a prospective cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 39 infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia, 13 of 26 assessed at 24 months (50%) showed sub-normative Bayley-4 performance in at least one domain despite only one having acute MRI-detected injury. Sub-normative performance was associated with higher postnatal base deficits and lactate levels and a trend toward less aEEG sleep-wake cycling.

papers.title: Region-Adapted Multi-Nutrient Supplementation in Chinese Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A 12-Week Pilot Randomised Controlled Trial.
papers.journal: Journal of nutritional science and vitaminology
papers.summary: In a 12-week pilot double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial of region-adapted multi-nutrient supplementation in 50 Chinese children with autism spectrum disorder, the primary Autism Behavior Checklist endpoint did not differ between groups, while exploratory analyses suggested improved receptive language alongside increased night waking and looser stools.

papers.title: Human iEEG recordings during audiovisual speech violations support and extend predictive routing models
papers.summary: Recorded intracranial EEG from superior temporal and prefrontal/premotor areas of seven presurgical epilepsy patients during an audiovisual speech paradigm to test predictive routing. Superior temporal cortex showed increased high-gamma and decreased alpha-beta power to auditory deviance and the McGurk condition, while frontal regions showed alpha-beta decreases without a high-gamma prediction error signal, and theta carried a strong prediction error signal in the McGurk condition—supporting and extending predictive routing models for human predictive processing.

papers.title: Effect of Preoperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 70 patients undergoing on-pump CABG, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine lowered 24-h hs-cTnT (170.29 vs 357.29 ng/L) and CK-MB, improved preoperative sleep quality, and reduced postoperative delirium incidence (14.3% vs 37.1%) without differing adverse events.

papers.title: Association of COVID-19 with neurodegenerative and neurological disorders in vaccinated and unvaccinated people
papers.summary: Using linked English primary care records from 18.3 million adults with up to 5.5 years follow-up, this study found elevated incidence of cognitive impairment and dementia shortly after COVID-19, with cognitive impairment incidence remaining elevated long term, particularly in unvaccinated and/or hospitalized individuals.

papers.title: Perimenopause and cardiometabolic risk: emerging evidence, therapeutic opportunities and unanswered questions.
papers.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
papers.summary: Reviews evidence that perimenopause is a convergence point where accelerated adverse changes in lipids, insulin sensitivity, body composition and vascular function coincide with vasomotor symptoms and sleep disturbance, with autonomic dysregulation, inflammation and neuroendocrine pathways proposed as shared mechanisms. Notes that whether these relationships are causal or therapeutically modifiable remains unresolved, as interventional studies in perimenopause are lacking.

papers.title: Effects of far-infrared radiation on the nervous system and their potential.
papers.summary: Reviews studies using animal models of nervous system disease to examine direct effects of far-infrared radiation (3-1000 μm, notably 8-14 μm) on the nervous system, covering memory impairment, cognitive function, neural regeneration, sleep, anti-inflammatory effects and stress relief. Attributes tissue effects to resonance with water molecules and resulting thermal and molecular modulation.

papers.title: Respiratory function, allergic reactions and quality of life in individuals working in container-like confined spaces after the 2023 Türkiye earthquakes: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 90 adults working at least two years in container-like confined spaces after the 2023 Türkiye earthquakes found relatively low FEV1% (68.9) and FVC% (64.1) with preserved FEV1/FVC (0.86), and mMRC dyspnea grade significantly associated with both FEV1% and FVC% (p<0.001). Fatigue independently predicted FEV1% and FEV1 in multivariable regression.

papers.title: Self-Reported Cannabis Use, Pain and Mental Health in People With Inheritable Bleeding Disorders.
papers.journal: Haemophilia : the official journal of the World Federation of Hemophilia
papers.summary: Cross-sectional analysis of registry data from 88 people with inheritable bleeding disorders found 25 (28.4%) reported cannabis use for symptom management, most often for pain, anxiety, sleep and depression, with highest perceived effectiveness for sleep (8.35), anxiety (7.06) and pain (6.36). Cannabis users had higher anxiety scores and significantly higher opioid use than non-users.

papers.title: The association between cardiovascular diseases and their risk factors in Austria and Slovakia: regression analyses based on the European Health Interview Survey (2019).
papers.journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
papers.summary: Weighted multivariable logistic regression of 2019 European Health Interview Survey data for adults aged ≥45 found CVD prevalence of 8.8% in Austria versus 15.3% in Slovakia. Sleep problems were associated with CVD in both countries (OR 1.90 Austria; 2.44 Slovakia), alongside hypertension and diabetes in Austria and diabetes and physical inactivity in Slovakia, with regional associations more pronounced in Austria.

papers.title: The neuropathic chameleon: we are hot on the scent.
papers.summary: This review discusses the heterogeneity of neuropathic pain and the need for mechanism-based classification to improve treatment development. It highlights candidate predictive and surrogate markers, focusing on sensory symptoms and signs assessed via patient-reported outcomes and sensory testing, for integration into future clinical trials.

papers.title: Preoperative Oral Esketamine for Perioperative Comfort in Children Undergoing Adenotonsillectomy: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Dose-Finding Study.
papers.summary: In a randomized double-blind dose-finding trial with 99 children undergoing adenotonsillectomy, preoperative oral esketamine at 1, 2, and 3 mg/kg improved sedation and analgesia at venous cannulation compared to control. The 2 mg/kg dose provided the best balance of efficacy and safety, while 3 mg/kg offered superior analgesia and opioid sparing.

papers.title: Longitudinal prediction of adolescent depression from environmental and polygenic risk scores.
papers.summary: Using data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study (N=9,797), this study developed a model predicting adolescent depression symptoms from environmental risk factors (depRS) and assessed its predictive value alone and combined with polygenic risk scores (PRS) for major depressive disorder at 2-year follow-up. The depRS model (12 predictors) explained 12.3% of variance, and combining depRS with PRS maximized classification accuracy (AUC up to 0.71).

papers.title: An integrative view of human nociceptor diversity: from microneurography to molecular identity.
papers.summary: This review integrates functional and molecular approaches to study human nociceptor diversity, discussing how microneurography-defined biophysical hallmarks can be transferred to in vitro patch-clamp paradigms and combined with Patch-seq to assign molecular identities to functionally defined nociceptor subtypes, such as mechano-insensitive 'sleeping' nociceptors. It highlights multimodal datasets linking electrophysiology, transcriptomics, and computational modeling to uncover ion channel mechanisms underlying pathological firing in neuropathic pain.

papers.title: Avoiding Diagnostic Pitfalls in Facial Pain: A Case Report of Paroxysmal Hemicrania Initially Treated as Trigeminal Neuralgia.
papers.summary: Reports a 21-year-old man with two-year recurrent strictly unilateral facial pain initially treated as trigeminal neuralgia with carbamazepine without benefit; attack duration and frequency, absent triggers, and restlessness suggested a trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia. A 14-day indomethacin trial (up to 225 mg daily) produced no improvement, so the diagnosis was recorded as probable paroxysmal hemicrania, and verapamil 240 mg daily was followed by marked reduction and eventual resolution of headache days, though causality cannot be established from a single uncontrolled case.

papers.title: Lived experiences and quality of life in people with severe, biologic-treated chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: a hermeneutic phenomenological study.
papers.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: This hermeneutic phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of 16 adults with severe, biologic-treated chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) from symptom onset through treatment failure. Three themes emerged: the silent burden of symptoms, the odyssey to obtain a diagnosis, and the experience of treatment failure and emotional strain, highlighting the substantial impact on quality of life and the role of family support.

papers.title: TruBlk™ Shilajit Resin Improves Sexual Function in Men with Erectile Dysfunction: A Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Trial
papers.summary: In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial of 100 men with mild-to-moderate erectile dysfunction, 90 days of standardised TruBlk Shilajit resin (250 mg twice daily) improved IIEF total score (+32.1% vs +13.6%) and raised total (+46.1% vs +10.0%) and free testosterone (+37.4% vs +6.8%), with reduced fatigue and, in exploratory subsets, improved sperm concentration and motility.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
